en.title: Iñárritu's Masterpiece 'Amores Perros' and More Hit Streaming This Week
en.summary: Dive into the latest streaming arrivals, including Alejandro G. Iñárritu's gritty debut and a chilling new thriller. Get ready for compelling narratives that span continents and genres.
en.body:
The streaming landscape is always evolving, and this week brings a compelling mix of critically acclaimed films and intriguing new series to our screens. For fans of visceral storytelling and directorial prowess, there's exciting news: Alejandro G. Iñárritu's seminal debut, **Amores Perros**, has arrived on MUBI. This 25th-anniversary 4K restoration offers a powerful look at the director's early genius, long before his Oscar-winning triumphs. The film masterfully weaves together three distinct narratives from the sprawling metropolis of Mexico City, all converging in a catastrophic car accident. Featuring a standout performance from **Gael García Bernal** and stunning cinematography by **Rodrigo Prieto**, **Amores Perros** remains a raw, unforgettable cinematic achievement that dissects the interconnectedness of fate and the human condition.

Beyond Iñárritu's masterpiece, another significant arrival is **The Furious**, now available on Hulu. Executive produced by **Liz Meriwether**, this series plunges viewers into a high-stakes cat-and-mouse game between an FBI agent, **Alice Black** (played by **Emmy Rossum**), and a cunning serial killer portrayed by **Lola Petticrew**. As their paths inevitably cross, the series promises to explore the blurring lines between justice and vengeance, offering a tense, character-driven thriller that will keep audiences on the edge of their seats.

## A Diverse Slate for Discerning Viewers

This week's new streaming content isn't limited to just one or two major releases. For those seeking different kinds of cinematic journeys, **Camp**, a VOD release, offers a poignant exploration of regret and trauma. The film centers on a young woman recounting a life-altering tragedy during a college party game, showcasing her journey toward acceptance and honesty. Meanwhile, Fatih Akin's **Amrum**, available on Kino Film Collection, presents a deeply personal story. Initially conceived by **Hark Bohm** as a self-directed project, Akin eventually took the reins on this film set on the island of Amrum during 1945, a place Bohm himself grew up on. The unique collaborative credit hints at the film's complex genesis and its intimate connection to its setting and history.

## What's Next on the Streaming Horizon

These recent additions underscore the breadth of compelling content accessible to global audiences. Whether you're drawn to the intense social commentary of **Amores Perros**, the thrilling pursuit in **The Furious**, the introspective drama of **Camp**, or the personal narrative of **Amrum**, there's something to captivate every viewer. Keep an eye on your favorite platforms for further announcements, as the world of streaming continues to deliver diverse and engaging stories throughout the year.

tr.title: Iñárritu'nun Ustalık Eseri 'Amores Perros' ve Daha Fazlası Bu Hafta İzlenebilir
tr.summary: Bu hafta, Alejandro G. Iñárritu'nun ilk filmi 'Amores Perros' ve yeni bir gerilim filmi dahil olmak üzere çeşitli içerikler izlenebiliyor. Farklı kıtalardan ve türlerden gelen hikayelerle dolu bir hafta olacak.
tr.body:
İzleme platformundaki içerikler her hafta değişiyor ve bu hafta da eleştirmenlerin beğenisini kazanan filmler ve yeni diziler izleyicilerle buluşuyor. Visceral hikayelere ve yönetmenlik yeteneğine meraklı olanlar için heyecan verici haberler var: Alejandro G. Iñárritu'nun ilk filmi 'Amores Perros', MUBI'de 25. yıl dönümü 4K restorasyonuyla izlenebiliyor. Bu film, yönetmenin erken dönemdeki dehasını güçlü bir şekilde gösteriyor ve Mexico City'deki üç farklı hikayeyi bir araya getiriyor. **Gael García Bernal**'in başarılı performansı ve **Rodrigo Prieto**'nun etkileyici sinematografisiyle 'Amores Perros', kader ve insan doğasının iç içeliğini inceleyen bir film olarak kalıyor.

 Iñárritu'nun ustalık eserinin yanı sıra, **The Furious** adlı dizi de Hulu'da izlenebiliyor. **Liz Meriwether**'in yapımcılığını yaptığı bu dizi, bir FBI ajanı **Alice Black** (oyuncu **Emmy Rossum**) ve bir seri katil (**Lola Petticrew**) arasında yüksek riskli bir kedi-fare oyununu anlatıyor. Adalet ve intikam arasındaki çizgileri keşfeden bu gerilim dolu dizi, izleyicileri koltuklarının kenarına çekecek.

## Çeşitli İzleme Seçenekleri
Bu haftanın yeni içerikleri sadece birkaç büyük yayınla sınırlı değil. Farklı türdeki sinematik yolculuklar arayanlar için **Camp**, bir VOD yayını olarak regret ve travma hakkında duygusal bir hikaye sunuyor. Film, bir kolej partisi oyununda bir kadın tarafından anlatılan bir yaşam değiştiren trajedi hakkında ve kabul ve dürüstlük yolculuğunu gösteriyor. Ayrıca, Fatih Akin'in **Amrum** filmi Kino Film Collection'da yer alıyor. İlk olarak **Hark Bohm** tarafından kendi projesi olarak düşünülen bu film, Akin tarafından yönetildi ve 1945 yılında Amrum adasında geçiyor. Bu benzersiz işbirliği, filmin karmaşık kökenini ve setting ve tarihiyle olan bağını gösteriyor.

## İzleme Gelecekte Neler Getirecek
Bu yeni eklemeler, global izleyicilere ulaşılabilir olan içeriklerin çeşitliliğini vurguluyor. **Amores Perros**'un sosyal yorumları, **The Furious**'ın heyecan verici kovalamacası, **Camp**'in introspektif dramı veya **Amrum**'un kişisel hikayesi size hitap ediyorsa, her izleyici için bir şeyler var. Favori platformlarınızı takip edin, çünkü izleme dünyası yıl boyunca çeşitli ve ilgi çekici hikayelerle dolu olacak.

content_raw: Each week we highlight the noteworthy titles that have recently hit streaming platforms in the United States. Check out this week’s selections below and past round-ups  here . Amores perros (Alejandro G. Iñárritu) Ahead of his Tom Cruise-led Digger arriving this fall, a 25th anniversary 4K restoration of Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s debut feature Amores perros is now streaming on MUBI. Led by Gael García Bernal and shot by Rodrigo Prieto, the triptych film, which follows three lives from disparate parts of Mexico City that converge in a fatal car crash, is still the director’s most accomplished. Where to Stream: MUBI Amrum (Fatih Akin) There’s a reason behind the odd credit at the start of  Amrum : “A Hark Bohm film by Fatih Akin.” While the two collaborated before on the latter’s  In the Fade , this project had a different beginning. Bohm wrote the script to direct himself before realizing he wouldn’t have the strength to do so. Raised on the island of Amrum (and a teen during the film’s 1945 setting), it was surely a very personal project that Akin initially refused to take over. – Jared M. ( full review ) Where to Stream: Kino Film Collection Camp (Avalon Fast) The opening credits reveal tragedy as a teenage Emily (Zola Grimmer) drives down a darkened country road only to hit and kill a young girl who ran into traffic chasing a soccer ball. It’s a reality she’s had to come to grips with over the years since, and, in a show of honesty, is the story she tells a bunch of strangers at a college party during a game of Truth or Dare: “What’s your biggest regret?” The clarity and confidence in relaying this fact proves she’s come out the other end. – Jared M. ( full review ) Where to Stream: VOD City Wide Fever (Josh Heaps) Whatever the last great horror movie was, I doubt it was so strange or compelling as  City Wide Fever . Shot on video, seemingly whenever the talent had free time from whatever else they were doing, this is a film rejects the eye-deadening digital that defines so many genre movies that go for prestige only to end up at TUBI. It’s also funny, with a sense of humor that is pranksterish, even juvenile without dipping into an edgelord attitude to which it could’ve so easily resorted. – Nick N. ( listen to his full interview with Josh Heaps ) Where to Stream: Fandor Faces of Death (Daniel Goldhaber) Director Daniel Goldhaber and co-writer Isa Mazzei are intimately familiar with the darker side of the Internet. Their 2018 debut,  Cam , remains among the quintessential horror films of the Internet age, and with their reboot / remake / reimagining of  Faces of Death , they bring the past into startling view of the present. It’s a film that recognizes there’s a little bit of a sicko in all of us, and there may be nothing we can do about it. – Devan S.
